family.template_note: families transplant reported score=8299/10000 (main:0808f1c0, Func_0808f1c0/BattleEffect start_effect_22). The template is real, useful compiler-shape evidence but is NOT this owner's algorithm: template looks up its resource via a real `bl` to ObjectTable_Get(Data_02000240[125]) (a fixed global index) and unconditionally flag-gates its EmitRandomParticleEffect callback assignment and two trailing Object_SetMode/Object_Destroy calls on `object`/`resource`; this owner instead (1) inlines the table lookup with its own `value` parameter as the index -- no `bl` to Func_0808ba1c/ObjectTable_Get appears anywhere in the retained assembly, (2) runs an extra 64-iteration pool-cleanup loop over the Data_03001e64-based EffectObject array (same 112-byte stride established in games/gs1/src/unidentified/main/runtime/runtime_owner_12.c and find_active_by_value.c's Work_08092be0.objects[]) gated on the *(s16*)(Data_03001ebc_value+0xCB8) 'active' flag already named in games/gs1/src/battle/effects/run_effect.c and scene_transition/reset.c, (3) transforms the spawn coordinates through an extra RotateVectorByMagnitude (Func_0800447c) call using an extra u16 resource field at offset 6 the template's EffectResource_0808f1c0 does not have, (4) calls Object_SetCallback(object, Data_0809e6c0) and writes object fields +0x28/+0x48 immediately after spawning -- the exact idiom from games/gs1/src/effect_runtime/run_rising_object_sequence.c's flags&1 branch, not present in the template at all, (5) sets object->callback = EmitRandomParticleEffect unconditionally at the end instead of the template's flags&1-gated assignment, and (6) is NOT void: it returns the spawned object pointer or NULL (both `movs r0,#0` early-exit sites and the final `adds r0,r7,#0` before return are present in the retained assembly), unlike the template's void Func_0808f1c0. Reused from the template only the byte-exact value_26/value_27=0, flags_a&=-33, and flags_b mask/clear/or shape, which alignment.json marks as a genuinely shared instruction block and which now compiles byte-identical here too.

register_gate_step4.decoder_signal: The reference uses r6 for the state base and then the loop counter, while r7 carries the resource pointer and then the transformed spawn-Z coordinate; the baseline represented all four phases as separate quantities and left the short resource quantity in r2.
register_gate_step4.source_edit: Represent the two non-overlapping r6 phases as state_or_count and the two non-overlapping r7 phases as resource_or_spawn_z, with ordinary integer/pointer conversions at the actual semantic boundaries.
register_gate_step4.compiler_effect: The paired carriers preserve the relative allocation priority: state/count occupies r6, resource/spawn-Z occupies r7 from the lookup onward, and r2 remains available for the global-cell address before GCC moves it into sl at the reference position.

rejected_experiments: Four declaration-order permutations for object/state/offset/resource/pos/spawn_x/spawn_z (object-first, resource-first, pos-first, and the final chosen order): all four produced byte-identical candidate output (same 11 differing halfwords, same r2-vs-r7 role). Consistent with games/gs1/recon/en/main/080a8c2c.json's traced finding that GCC 2.96's local-alloc.c qty_compare tie-break is governed by RTL discovery order within a basic block, not C declaration/statement order.

Removing the `u32 offset = (value*4)+0x14;` intermediate (inlining the expression directly into the pointer cast): regressed candidate_bytes from 344 to 348 and differing_halfwords from 11 to 14 -- the intermediate variable is required to reproduce the reference's exact `lsls r0,r0,#2 / ldr r6,[r2,#0] / adds r0,#20 / ldr r7,[r6,r0]` instruction selection (get.c's own `offset = (arg0*4)+0x14; return *(void**)(base+offset);` shape). Kept.

Rewriting the table lookup as array indexing (`struct EffectResource_0808ef70 **table = (...)(state+0x14); resource = table[value];`) instead of pointer-plus-offset: regressed sharply to candidate=348/dh=168 -- the compiler chose a completely different (worse) address-computation shape. Reverted.

Introducing a `u8 **globalSlot = (u8**)&Data_03001ebc;` intermediate for the shared address (matching scene_transition/reset.c's own `globalSlot` idiom) vs referencing `&Data_03001ebc` directly at both use sites: byte-identical either way (CSE recognizes the reuse regardless of source spelling). Kept the simpler direct-reference form.

Routing the table-lookup result through an untyped `void *lookup` local before assigning to the typed `resource` pointer, to see if a generic-pointer pseudo changed RTL discovery order ahead of the typed one: no effect (identical 11-diff output). Reverted to the direct typed assignment.

Spelling the halfword merge's keep-mask as `~0x3FF` instead of `0xFFFFFC00`, and as a separately-declared `u32 keep_mask` local, and via an intermediate `u32 existing` read-then-write, and via a `s32 packed` intermediate for the Func_08003fa4 term: all either no-op'd or regressed (up to candidate=364/dh=122) versus the plain inline expression. None reproduced the reference's pool-loaded 0xFFFFFC00 constant -- GCC's optimizer recognized the AND was redundant on a zero-extended 16-bit load and narrowed it to the 8-bit-rotated immediate 0xFC00 (movs+lsls) regardless of spelling, matching this session's other documented finding that same-valued-constant folding is value-driven, not text-driven.

Swapping the OR operand order in the halfword merge (mask-term first vs call-term first): the call-term-first ordering matched the reference's `ands r0,r3` (0x3FF load) placement and dropped differing_halfwords from 45 to 43 before the bitfield fix below; kept.

A static inline lookup helper, splitting resource declaration from assignment, and introducing a post-guard typed alias were all optimized back to the 11-halfword baseline. Copying the position as an aggregate regressed to 133 differing halfwords.

Merging only resource with spawn_z, including a short typed-copy boundary intended to encourage coalescing, produced 16 differing halfwords: the longer merged quantity took r6 and displaced state into r7. That negative result exposed the missing paired lifetime rather than supporting a one-sided carrier repair.
notes: Recovered only from the retained owner assembly (games/gs1/asm/0808ef70.s), the family-transplant workspace's m2c output run against the target's own object (out/family-transplants/main-0808ef70/m2c/0808ef70.c and target.canonical.s), the byte-exact template games/gs1/src/battle/effects/objects/start_effect_22.c, the already-adopted sibling sources games/gs1/src/object/table/get.c, games/gs1/src/object/table/find_active_by_value.c, games/gs1/src/battle/effects/run_effect.c, games/gs1/src/battle/effects/scene_transition/reset.c, games/gs1/src/battle/effects/interpolate/prepare.c, games/gs1/src/effect_runtime/is_active.c, games/gs1/src/effect_runtime/run_rising_object_sequence.c, games/gs1/src/battle/effects/random_particle/emit.c and spawn_at_position.c, the lower-confidence in-repo candidate games/gs1/src/unidentified/main/runtime/runtime_owner_12.c (for the Data_03001e64/112-byte-stride array naming precedent), games/gs1/include/types.h and global_cells.h, and the approved compiler. No GS2 evidence, external source, another decompilation project, copied instruction bytes, fixed-register variable, inline assembly, compiler barrier, or compiler modification was used.

The single biggest structural discovery this pass: the u16 field at visual+8 (which straddles the template's `unknown_06[3]`/`flags_b` boundary) is written back with `field = (field & 0xFFFFFC00) | (Func_08003fa4(...) & 0x3FF)` in the reference, but writing that literally as manual masking let GCC's optimizer narrow the redundant upper bits of the AND-mask down to the smaller immediate 0xFC00 (movs+lsls instead of a pool load), which the reference never does. Declaring the field as a genuine C89 10-bit bitfield instead (`struct PackedField08_0808ef70 { u16 value : 10; };`, assigned directly with no manual mask) let GCC's own bitfield read-modify-write codegen materialize the full 32-bit complement mask exactly as the reference's literal pool does, and dropped differing_halfwords from 43 to 11 in one change -- this is genuine source-shape recovery, not forcing: bitfields are ordinary C, and the container width (u16) matches the reference's confirmed `ldrh`/`strh` access width.

A second structural discovery: this owner's `if (object != 0) { ... }` wrapping had to become two independent early returns (`if (resource == 0) return 0;` ... `if (object == 0) return 0;`) rather than nested ifs to reproduce the reference's two separate `movs r0,#0` default-return-value materializations and the `adds r0,r7,#0` reload immediately before the first Object_SetCallback call -- a single `object = 0;`-initialized-then-conditionally-overwritten variable let the compiler keep r0 alive across the whole function and never needed to reload it, which is legitimately correct code but not what the reference did. This also required scoping `visual`/`handle`/`mask`/`zero` into a nested block declared with `visual`'s declaration doubling as its initializer (`struct EffectVisual_0808ef70 *visual = object->visual;`) placed AFTER the Object_SetCallback call rather than at the top of a larger block -- putting all four locals together at the top of one big block raised register pressure enough to spill a 4th high register (fp) into the prologue (candidate grew to 354/364 bytes with an extra push{r7}/pop{r7} pair), which the reference's 3-high-register prologue never has.

Confirmed by direct assembly reading (not assumed) that the value-parameter is used directly as the object-table index with no `bl` to Func_0808ba1c/ObjectTable_Get anywhere in games/gs1/asm/0808ef70.s -- the lookup is fully inlined as `*(u8**)(*(u8**)Data_03001ebc + (value*4) + 0x14)`, matching object/table/get.c's own formula exactly but without the function call. Confirmed the pool-cleanup loop's base pointer at Data_03001ebc-88 (0x03001e64) via direct arithmetic on the retained `mov r3,sl; subs r3,#88` and cross-checked it against the identical Data_03001e64/112-byte-stride/64-entry array already named in runtime_owner_12.c. Confirmed 0x0808f28d/0x0808eee5 resolve (thumb-bit-set) to the already-adopted BattleEffect_SpawnRandomParticleAtPosition (games/gs1/src/battle/effects/random_particle/spawn_at_position.c, owner main:0808f28c) and EmitRandomParticleEffect (games/gs1/src/battle/effects/random_particle/emit.c, owner main:0808eee4) respectively via games/gs1/source-paths.json, and that 0x0809e87c/0x0809e6c0 are the already-named data markers Data_0809e87c and Data_0809e6c0 used exactly this way (as a stale-callback sentinel and an Object_SetCallback argument, respectively) in emit.c/spawn_at_position.c and run_rising_object_sequence.c.

The former 11-differing-halfword/12-wrong-instruction residual (class=allocation) was entirely register-role assignment for the resource pointer (r2 in the baseline candidate versus r7 in the reference), plus the resulting placement of `mov sl,r2`. Single-variable aliases and declaration changes did not move it because they did not alter the competing lifetime topology.

Reading the reference register phases exposed the complete repair: r6 carries the state base before becoming the loop counter, and r7 carries the resource pointer before becoming spawn_z. Expressing both disjoint pairs as the ordinary C carriers state_or_count and resource_or_spawn_z closed the owner from 11 to zero differing halfwords; expressing only the r7 pair regressed to 16 because it stole r6. No register-qualified local, named-register variable, inline assembly, compiler flag override, scheduling control, compiler patch, or hand-authored instruction byte was used.

Adoption gate met on 2026-08-28: two isolated fresh compilations and the production-named source each measured 344/344 bytes with zero differing halfwords. tools/check integrate accepted the owner, installed games/gs1/src/battle/effects/random_particle/start_emitter.c, and retired games/gs1/asm/0808ef70.s.
